title: SAND2010-7594 A516 carbon steel corrosion
summary:
- Corrosion study on A516 carbon steel in molten nitrate salt.
- Chloride content affects corrosion rate and scale adherence.
- Magnetite is the primary corrosion product.
- Corrosion rates increase with chloride concentration.
- Temperature influences corrosion behavior.
- Corrosion tests conducted on A516 Grade 70 carbon steel in molten binary Solar Salt.
- Chloride concentrations of 0, 0.5, and 1.0 wt.% were investigated.
- Corrosion rates determined by descaled weight losses.
- X-ray diffraction used to determine types of corrosion products.
- Metallographic examination for corrosion morphology.
- Corrosion rates measured using gravimetric data and extrapolated to annual loss rates.
- XRD used to identify oxidation products on A516 steel coupons.
summary_points: Corrosion study on A516 carbon steel in molten nitrate salt.
Chloride content affects corrosion rate and scale adherence.
Magnetite is the primary corrosion product.
Corrosion rates increase with chloride concentration.
Temperature influences corrosion behavior.
Corrosion tests conducted on A516 Grade 70 carbon steel in molten binary Solar Salt.
Chloride concentrations of 0, 0.5, and 1.0 wt.% were investigated.
Corrosion rates determined by descaled weight losses.
X-ray diffraction used to determine types of corrosion products.
Metallographic examination for corrosion morphology.
Corrosion rates measured using gravimetric data and extrapolated to annual loss rates.
XRD used to identify oxidation products on A516 steel coupons.
Chloride content and temperature significantly affect corrosion rates.
Net weight changes monitored for qualitative insights into the corrosion process.
La corrosión del acero al carbón se ve afectada por la temperatura y el contenido de cloruro en los salines moltenos.
Las capas óxidas alcanzan un grosor dado más rápidamente a temperaturas más altas debido al Piling-Bedworth ratio.
El análisis XRD reveló que la única óxida formada fue magnetita (Fe3O4).
Los examenes metalográficos mostraron porosidad y fracturas internas en las capas óxidas formadas a 450°C.
Metal loss rates at 400°C and 450°C are insufficient for establishing temperature dependence of corrosion.
Data from other long-term tests help establish a better understanding of temperature dependence.
Corrosion rates of carbon steel in chloride-free molten salts fit an Arrhenius equation with an activation energy of 30.5 kcal.
Magnetite is the primary corrosion product at temperatures between 300°C and 550°C.
Chloride impurities affect corrosion rates, increasing metal losses at higher concentrations.
References to various studies on iron-carbon alloy oxidation.
Distribution list includes multiple authors and institutions from the U.S. Department of Energy and National Renewable Energy Laboratory.
